extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (PIs, postdocs, early-career investigators) seeking funding/resubmission guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, mechanism-specific advice and procedural standards for NIH extramural grant submissions, resubmissions, IC/SRG assignment, paylines, JIT/administrative review, and award timing. Includes mechanism examples (R01, R03, R15, K-series, R35/MIRA, SBIR/STTR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payline and Continuing Resolution (CR) effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim paylines during a CR are conservative and will not be adjusted until after the federal budget is signed into law; final paylines are set only after ICs receive appropriations and are retroactive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs will not have final paylines until after the FY budget is signed into law; ICs typically receive their appropriations ~6–8 weeks after that, and paylines may be adjusted thereafter (sometimes after Council). During a CR paylines are often held flat (this year CR funding was same as FY21), which can delay or delay clarity on awards. Expect adjustments (if any) some weeks/months after law passage; being on an interim paylist is not a guarantee of funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Being on a ranked paylist is not a guarantee of funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Placement on an IC's ranked paylist or being within an interim payline does not guarantee an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After Council, the IC Director establishes a ranked paylist, but being on the list can take weeks and is not a guarantee. Even apps within the payline can be skipped for specific reasons (see 'Reasons applications are skipped'). POs may recommend resubmission while payline/funding clarity is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons an application within the payline may be skipped
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that appear fundable can nonetheless be bypassed for award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common reasons include: the PI is already too well funded; the PI secured other funding for the same work since review; major unresolved changes in PI/key personnel; administrative or ethical issues that cannot be resolved. Also institutional/IC portfolio constraints (oversubscription in particular area) can lead to skipping.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC assignment and changing IC on resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: You may change the IC when resubmitting; IC assignment is based on the science and the willingness of an IC to accept the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since CSR/CSR Assisted Referral Tool (ART) and CSR contacts ICs based on your abstract/aims, you can suggest an IC but do not get to unilaterally pick one. If you want to change ICs, ask the target IC PO whether they'd accept it and be prepared to convince both ICs that the science fits their mission. Complete the PHS Assignment Request Form (part of the application package) and use a cover letter to name a PO with whom you've worked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study section (SRG) selection and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose the SRG/study section based on who would be excited about your science and which panel's expertise and history aligns with your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RePORTER Matchmaker and CSR Assisted Referral Tool (ART) to identify recommended SRGs and POs. Check past funded applications from that SRG, current roster, and whether panel members are in your field. If reviewed in an SEP, consult the prospective IC PO about SRG fit and whether A0 vs A1 route is better when changing panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation and use of the Summary of Discussion / Resume
rubrics_metrics.description: The Summary of Discussion and the Resume (summary of panel concerns/strengths) represent the score-driving issues and should be the focus when revising an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize addressing the weaknesses identified in the Summary of Discussion rather than every point in individual critiques, since the SRO's Summary captures what drove the score. For applications not discussed, pay attention to primary reviewer critiques. Use experienced, critical colleagues (even the harshest reviewer you can find) to mimic study section scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and limits of Program Officer (PO)
rubrics_metrics.description: POs can advise (e.g., recommend resubmission, suggest whether to wait) and provide insight into likely outcomes, but they do not process awards and cannot always predict timing or guarantee funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs may suggest addressing reviewer comments or advise waiting vs resubmitting, but award processing is handled by grants management/GMO and funding decisions are formally made by Institute Directors (often delegated to Division Directors). If a PO is unresponsive, escalate politely by copying the division director or Director of DER; institutional grants administrators can sometimes expedite communications with the GMO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative review / JIT / 'Pending administrative review' status
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Pending administrative review' usually indicates the IC is reviewing an application for possible award (administrative/GM checks), not a guarantee but a positive sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status changes like 'Pending administrative review' or 'Award prepared' mean the application is under grants management review and is likely to be funded barring issues. However, award issuance can still be delayed by budget constraints/CR or outstanding administrative items requested via JIT (e.g., IACUC, degree documentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'Award prepared' and NOA timing
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Award prepared' indicates award terms are ready and NOA issuance is imminent, though timing can still be delayed by processing queues or budget issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically the gap between 'Award prepared' and NOA is a few days to a few weeks; in some cases (e.g., year-end or CR-induced backlog) it may be longer. 'Award prepared' often means the check is in the mail; awards have been issued even without a finalized federal budget in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing expectations from Council to NOA
rubrics_metrics.description: From Council action to the Notice of Award (NOA) can take weeks to months, with variability by IC, mechanism, and fiscal situation (CRs, appropriations delays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example timelines from community posts: Council completion to NOA can be months; if budget bills are delayed, ICs wait for appropriations (~6–8 weeks after law) before finalizing paylines and many awards. Plan accordingly and consider resubmitting if timelines jeopardize career milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission strategy and handling prior critiques (mechanism-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmission approach depends on mechanism and current PAR rules (e.g., some PARs do not allow A1 amendments for R35/MIRA, requiring a new application without referencing prior submission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For standard A1 resubmissions, explicitly address score-driving weaknesses and the Summary of Discussion. For PARs that disallow A1 (e.g., current R35 PAR cited), submit a new application with no reference to prior submission and ask the PO whether to submit to the last date or wait for the next PAR. Ask the PO whether a new submission is advised mid-cycle (e.g., by mid-March for a May deadline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on holding certain awards (R15/AREA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific mechanisms impose PI-holding limits (e.g., you can only hold one R15 as PI at a time), though you may serve as co-investigator on others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If timing is tight, consult your PO to determine whether to be PI or a co-investigator on a new submission. Administrative rules vary by mechanism; check the Funding Opportunity Announcement and ask your PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: MIRA/R35 funding decision factors
rubrics_metrics.description: NIGMS MIRA (R35) funding decisions are holistic: score is important but PI situation, area of science, ESI status, and IC priorities influence timing and selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIGMS historically uses a mix of impact score and programmatic considerations; POs can provide context but funding decisions are made by the Institute/Division leadership. For ESIs, timing (e.g., tenure decisions) can affect prioritization. Consult MIRA score spreadsheets/discussions and your PO for targeted advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation and communication strategies when PO is unresponsive
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PO doesn't respond to substantive queries (e.g., resubmission advice), escalate politely and provide context by copying relevant supervisors or senior management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include: reply-all to prior messages to provide context, copy the Director of the Division of Extramural Research, contact branch/division/group chief, have your PI or institutional grants administrator contact the GMO directly (PI pressure can help), and use RePORTER/Matchmaker outputs to find alternative POs to consult.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC budget management and end-of-year adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs may manage limited appropriations by stretching dollars across awards or reducing noncompetitive budgets rather than sharply changing paylines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include cutting noncompetitive budgets by ~5–10% during tight funding years, or trimming award amounts late in the fiscal year to fund more applications. If awarded amounts appear reduced, discuss reallocations with your PO and consider supplement requests for critical needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to prepare contingency/resubmission applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a resubmission (or a new application) as insurance when funding timelines are uncertain or if the PO advises so, especially when PARs have impending deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If POs are noncommittal or appropriations appear delayed, start working on a backup application (even at low intensity) so you can meet upcoming deadlines (e.g., May 17 PAR cutoff). If an earlier application is funded, the duplicate/new app can be administratively withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of portfolio/search tools to identify appropriate POs/SRGs
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage online tools (RePORTER Matchmaker, CSR ART) to find POs, SRGs, and activity codes that historically fund similar science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paste your abstract/Specific Aims into Matchmaker/ART to get ranked lists of POs and SRGs. Then review PO portfolios and SRG past funded apps to assess fit and to choose targets for cover letters and assignment requests.
